glossary.Inflammation: The body's response to injury or infection, causing swelling and redness.
glossary.Airway lining: The layer of cells covering the inside of the airways.
glossary.Influenza: The flu virus, causing fever, aches and cough.
glossary.Coronavirus: A family of viruses causing colds and COVID-19.
glossary.Persistent cough: A cough that goes on for weeks.
glossary.Non-productive cough: A dry cough with no sputum.
glossary.Productive cough: A cough that brings up sputum.
glossary.Sputum: Mucus coughed up from the lower airways.
glossary.Auscultation: Listening to the chest with a stethoscope.
glossary.Secondary bacterial infection: A bacterial infection that takes hold after a virus has damaged the airway.
glossary.Breathlessness: Difficulty breathing or feeling short of breath.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination without needing tests.
glossary.Chest X-ray: Plain X-ray of the chest, used here to look for pneumonia.
glossary.Reassurance: Explaining the illness is usually mild and self-limiting.
glossary.Self-care: Things patients do themselves, such as rest, fluids and simple painkillers.
glossary.Supportive measures: Treatment that eases symptoms while the body clears the infection.
glossary.Paracetamol: A simple painkiller that also lowers fever.
glossary.Cough suppressant: A medicine that reduces the urge to cough.
glossary.Asthma: A condition of reversible airway narrowing and wheeze.
glossary.Antibiotics: Drugs that kill or stop bacteria; they do not work on viruses.
glossary.Type 2 diabetes: Diabetes from insulin resistance, which raises infection risk.
glossary.Heart failure: The heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.
glossary.Epithelium: The layer of cells lining a surface, here the inside of the airways.
glossary.Mucus: Sticky fluid made by the airway lining to trap particles.
glossary.Sputum production: Making and coughing up mucus from the airways.
glossary.Self-limiting: Gets better on its own without treatment.
